judgments.rationale: The element is the 'Saiba mais' button (<a href="" target="" class="cta mt-5">) under 'Conheça a Santa Casa JF'. The live HTML fetched on 2026-11-21 and the styled screenshot match the snapshot for this element, including the empty href; no script on the page handles it, so activating it only reloads the home page. The claim says nothing around the link tells where it goes, but the h2 'Conheça a Santa Casa JF' is the nearest heading before it, which this round counts as context, so 'Saiba mais' reads as 'learn more about the Santa Casa JF': the ground the claim gives does not hold. What remains is that the href is empty, a placeholder link that leads back to the page itself. Whether such a dead link fails 2.4.4 (its real effect, a reload, is not what text and heading promise) or is a broken link that 2.4.4 does not cover is something competent auditors would split on. They would also split on whether this generic 'no context' claim, made without Rampa reading the destination, names that defect. So I do not confirm it and label it uncertain.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Icon in the 'Resultados de exames' card link. The live HTML fetched on 2026-11-21 and the styled screenshot match the snapshot for this element. The image is an icon at the top of a card link whose own text (an h3 heading and a paragraph) already gives the link's purpose, so the icon only illustrates that text. I looked for something that would make it pass: no aria-hidden, no role=presentation, no null alt, no other name source. Its alt "ícone" ("icon") is a placeholder word, not a file name, so the claim's disjunction holds. An illustrative icon next to text that says the same should be ignored by assistive technology (alt=""), and F39 names exactly this as a 1.1.1 failure, with alt="image" as its example; read as an informative image it fails F30 instead (placeholder text). Either way screen readers announce a meaningless "ícone" inside the link, which is what the claim points at. No reason that the element passes held up.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The 'Comunicado' category label on the second news card. The live HTML fetched on 2026-11-21 and the styled screenshot match the snapshot for this element. The theme's style.css (.blog .posts .box .texto span) sets color #FFF on background #0078D7, font-size .9em (14.4px at the 16px default), weight 500, uppercase, so the pixel measurement matches the CSS: the ratio is 4.499:1. The text is not large (under 18pt, and not 14pt bold), so 4.5:1 applies, and Understanding 1.4.3 says the computed value is not rounded ("4.499:1 would not meet the 4.5:1 threshold"). I checked whether the page's 'Contraste' toggle could make it pass by G174: its script adds .bgdark to body and #home .blog and .textdark to p, a, h1-h5 and li, but leaves this span's own #0078D7 background and #FFF text unchanged, so the alternate presentation keeps 4.499:1. The label is real text, not a logo or an inactive control. The claim states the right colours and a ratio just under 4.5:1 ('at most 4.49' is the truncated 4.499), and the element fails 1.4.3.
